main_text.l: scandalis, serva literarum studia, tuere docentium & discentium coetus. Excita, illumina, & rege spi-ritu tuo, & defende pios gubernatores & salu-tares, qui Ecclesiam foveant & promoveant: inpri-mis autem Illustrissimum nostrum Principem & Dominum, Dn. Johannem Casimirum, Comitem Palatinum, Ducem Bavariæ & Electo-ralis Palatinatus tutorem & administratorem, u-nà cum Illustrissimo pupillo, reliquisque do-mus Palatinæ Principibus, rege gratia & veritate tua, ut te recte agnoscant, & concordi studio fe-licique successu regnum tuum promoveant.

Concede illis tranquillitatem, & gubernationem Patriæ & Ecclesiæ salutarem. Denique redde nos omnes per Spiritum συμφύτες[?] τῷ ὁμοιώματι τοῦ θανάτου[?], καὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως[?] ἐς[?], & da, ut in hac æru-mnosa vita peccatis moriamur, & ad novam vitam resurgamus, in qua non nobis, sed tibi viva-mus, expectantes secundam resurrectionem, in qua conformes tibi facti, tecum regnemus in omnem æternitatem.

page.notes: The Greek phrase (Rom. 6:5) is only partly legible in the scan; the marked words and endings are doubtful. The faint mirrored text below the main text is show-through from the reverse side and is left out. The left edge of the first line is cut off, so the opening word is read as "scandalis" from its visible letters.
